newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Arianespace to launch Malaysia's second satellite.
newsitem.headline: Arianespace to launch Malaysia's second satellite.

text.p: The European space consortium Arianespace said on Friday it will launch Malaysia's second satellite into orbit on November 13.

The launch of the second Malaysia East Asia Satellite (Measat-2) comes 10 months after the first was placed into orbit from the launch site at Kourou in French Guiana, Arianespace sales manager Richard Bowles told reporters at a briefing.
Measat's owner, Binariang Sdn Bhd, will begin a direct-to-user satellite television service next month for Malaysians, featuring 22 digital television and eight radio channels.
The satellite also provides services for Binariang's telecommunications company.
Hughes Space and Communications is manufacturing both Measat satellites at a cost of $235 million each.
Measat Broadcast, the media arm of Binariang, said earlier this week the satellites' footprint stretches from the Indian subcontinent to the Philippines and from southern China to eastern Australia.
The company said it plans to launch a third satellite in 1998 that will allow it to produce hundreds of channels for broadcast into niche markets around the world.
Bowles said the Asia-Pacific region has become one of the most important markets for satellites.
